links.outcome: Usability issues identified and resolved through iterative interface testing with oncologists
links.effect: Across 5 design rounds including 13 oncologist interviews, usability testing confirmed that earlier issues were resolved and identified further needed enhancements (e.g., use months not days) and usability and trust concerns.
links.quote: Qualitative findings confirmed that previously identified issues were resolved and clarified necessary enhancements (eg, use months not days) and concerns about usability and trust (eg, address LoT received elsewhere).

unlisted_practices: Iterative user-centered design of an interface for communicating ML-based prognosis, with ongoing oncologist input
Expert review of the interface against usability heuristics
Input from a color-blind adult on the interface design
Favoring interpretability over explainability in prognosis displays
Restricting appropriate use of prognosis output to the context of a conversation with an oncologist

screen.reason: Empirical user-centered design and qualitative evaluation study assessing the design of a clinical interface to communicate ML-based prognostic risk to oncologists using vignettes and iterative feedback.

primary.practice: user-centered interface design for prognostic communication
